b.boardwalk.1: A 12-tile wooden path from the island across the first creek. 30% faster to walk, and it stays dry until the tide is nearly full.
b.boardwalk.2: Extend it to 28 tiles, across the second creek. Ride it home even from the far sandbars.
b.boardwalk.3: Extend it to 43 tiles, past the deep channel to the horizon sandbar.
b.cottage.1: Sew a bigger sack at home. Carry weight 10 → 14.
b.cottage.2: An even bigger sack. Carry weight 14 → 18.
b.cottage.3: A sturdy big sack. Carry weight 18 → 24.
b.haenyeo.1: Grandma the diver moves in. Help with her 3 daily requests for gifts, and she'll give advice when you're stuck.
b.shed.1: Ride a mud sled on mud. Speed on mud 60% → 100%.
b.shed.2: A smoother sled. Speed on mud 100% → 120%.
b.lighthouse.1: Clears the sea fog so you can see what's on the far sandbars. Rings a bell when it's time to head back.
b.lighthouse.2: When the bell rings, its light shows the fastest way home.
b.stilt.1: A shelter on the far sandbar. Reach its ladder and the boatman rows you home.
b.next_run: Your next tide will be different

set.credits_text:
Font: Galmuri (SIL Open Font License 1.1, Lee Minseo)
Art, sound and music were made for this game.
t.coin.d: A coin with a hole. What did it buy?
t.marble.d: Children rolled these across the flats.
t.whistle.d: Once used to call the tide.
t.teacup.d: It still smells faintly of tea.
t.pen.d: Maybe it wrote the bottled letters.
t.model.d: A tiny model of the old lighthouse.
letter.l1: There was a village on this island once. People who knew the tides lived here.
letter.l2: On spring tides you could walk all the way to the horizon.
letter.l3: Greed doesn't weigh down the sack. It weighs down your ankles.
letter.l4: When the lighthouse went dark, everyone left.
letter.l5: The creeks always fill first. Watch the way back.
letter.l6: If someone lays the boardwalk again, we'll come home.
letter.l7: We built a hut on the far sandbar. The boatman always waited.
letter.l8: To whoever reads this: thank you for bringing the island back.
